about.title: Trinidad Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Trinidad is a small coastal town, but the roads that run through and around it — US-101, Scenic Drive, Patricks Point Drive, and the Trinidad Frontage Road — carry a steady mix of local traffic, commuters, and visitors heading toward the coast. Public crash records show these corridors account for the bulk of reported collisions here, with Monday mornings between 9 and 11 a.m. showing up more often than other times. Even a single injury collision, like the one recorded most recently, can leave someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster asking for a recorded statement before they've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects people hurt in Trinidad-area crashes with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the claim, deal with insurers, and explain options under California law. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Trinidad Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Move Faster Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government entity or road agency may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Connecting early with an attorney helps make sure a Trinidad-area claim doesn't miss a critical filing date.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you're partly responsible for a crash on roads like the Trinidad Frontage Road. An independent attorney can help make sure fault is assessed fairly rather than accepted at the insurer's first offer.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, But No Guarantees Either
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. That said, results depend on the facts of each claim — an attorney can walk through what's realistic before any recorded statement is given to the other driver's insurer.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since insurers often use those statements to minimize a claim later. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on what to say and what to hold off on. This is especially important soon after a crash when you may still be shaken up or unsure of your injuries.

items.question: What if my crash happened on US-101 near Trinidad instead of in town?
items.answer: It doesn't matter whether the collision happened on the highway corridor or on a local road like Scenic Drive or Patricks Point Drive — what matters is where you live, where you were treated, and where the crash occurred for jurisdiction purposes. An attorney can sort out the right venue and applicable rules. LawProactive can still connect you with someone familiar with Humboldt County claims either way.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: There's no cost to you at any point. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. You're never obligated to hire anyone after being connected.
